title: Dynamic token staging and kernel hinting for heterogeneous multi-GPU scheduling
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Tail latency and cost variability on heterogeneous GPU fleets are largely driven by suboptimal coordination between prefill and decode phases, per-device kernel choices, and serialized all-reduce windows. This ticket proposes a runtime-level scheduling primitive that stages token work across devices with explicit priority lanes and propagates lightweight kernel-selection hints so compute and comms overlap is maximized without violating latency SLOs. Goals: 1) Reduce 95/99th latency for interactive requests by overlapping NCCL collectives with non-blocking per-device compute; 2) Reduce wasted kernel launches by steering small, latency-sensitive token waves to low-latency kernels and batching-friendly waves to throughput kernels; 3) Preserve deterministic decode ordering and KV cache correctness across tensor/pipeline parallel partitions.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile decode latency improved by >= 20% for interactive workloads (internal latency dashboard measurement)
Average GPU utilization for mixed workload increases by >= 10% while token-cost per request does not increase > 5%
Unit tests cover token staging queue, priority lane demotion/promotion, and kernel hint flow
Canary rollout on dedicated cluster with heterogeneous GPUs (A100 + A30 example) shows stable SLOs for 48h
No regression in correctness: KV cache state is identical to baseline for deterministic replay tests
technical_design: Overview: Introduce a light-weight Token Staging Layer (TSL) in the conductor that sits between the request dispatcher and per-device executor. TSL maintains short-lived micro-queues per device and a global priority arbiter. Each token wave (prefill batch or decode step) carries metadata: request_priority (interactive|background), estimated_seq_len, and kernel_hint (latency|throughput|mixed). Kernel_hint is derived from sequence-length heuristics, model-config lookup, and recent latency telemetry. Scheduling: 1) Priority arbiter admits latency-sensitive waves immediately into low-latency kernel lanes with size caps to avoid head-of-line blocking. 2) Background/throughput waves are aggregated into size-bound micro-batches that favor throughput-optimized kernels and quantized execution paths. 3) When a device enters a communication window (NCCL all-reduce for KV exchange), the TSL attempts to overlap remaining local compute (attention fusion kernels) with the collective by reordering admitted waves so that compute-heavy kernels run during NCCL. Implementation details: - Kernel hint propagation: conductor annotates the CUDA stream/task with hint tokens; per-device runtime chooses kernel variant using a two-level lookup (model + hint + recent_exec_profile). - NCCL overlap strategy: dynamic window sizing based on measured inter-device skew; when skew > threshold, schedule small latency waves on devices ahead to consume slack while collective completes elsewhere. - Backpressure/fallback: if staging queues grow beyond threshold, demote background waves and force immediate microbatch flushes. - Correctness: attach sequence checksums to waves to validate KV cache updates post-collective. - Telemetry hooks: emit per-wave timing, kernel variant chosen, NCCL overlap ratio, queue depth to runtime metrics.
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype TSL data structures and kernel_hint propagation (2 dev days)
PR: conductor + per-device runtime minimal API changes to accept kernel_hint and staging operations
Perf harness: synthetic mixed workload (chatty interactive + bulk embeddings) to measure overlap and tail latency
Iterate kernel selection policy: implement fallback rules and a simple EWMA-based execution profile store
Safety: add KV cache checksum validation and unit/integration tests
Canary rollout: enable feature flag on dedicated cluster, monitor for 48h, collect traces
Rollout: phase gates -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% of dedicated clusters after observability validation
test_plan: Unit tests: token staging enqueue/dequeue, priority promotion/demotion, kernel_hint encoding/decoding
Integration test: multi-GPU prefill/decode replay with deterministic seeds to compare KV cache and outputs
Performance test: A/B against baseline using our latency suite (50k requests) measuring p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization
Chaos: inject delayed NCCL windows on one device to validate that TSL consumes slack without violating ordering
Stability: 48h canary with production-like request mix and health alerts (error rate, queue depth)
Benchmark: quantify additional overhead introduced by TSL (target < 0.5ms median scheduling overhead)
Security/regression: ensure no new surface for data leakage between isolated tenants (run isolation tests)
rollout_plan: Day-0: internal canary on non-prod dedicated cluster with synthetic traffic
Day-3: canary to small subset of prod-dedicated clusters (10%) with close monitoring
Day-7: expand to 50% if metrics meet acceptance criteria
Full: enable on all dedicated clusters after two successful windows and sign-off from SRE/Perf
Post-rollout: 2-week observation period with weekly rollback gates
risks: Scheduling overhead could increase median latency if micro-queue management is inefficient
Incorrect kernel hints may harm throughput for certain model configs until policy is tuned
Complexity in overlapping NCCL could hide rare correctness bugs in KV updates
Edge cases with very heterogeneous device speeds may require fallback to conservative policies
Feature interacts with autoscaling and burst capacity logic; need to ensure it doesn't prevent scale-outs
